topology_counts.counting_rule: Count publication carrier families, production publication paths, install entrypoints, runtime forms, and payload densities separately; never add them into one total.

windows_x64_rc_preview.rule: The current public Windows RC is a manual opt-in WSL2-only Preview with exact release-byte terminal acceptance. Every Codex-backed route remains bound to one Linux executor identity with no native Windows fallback; Latest, Stable updater, Homebrew, and Stable Bundle admission remain forbidden.

distribution_semantics.rule: quality_status, build_trigger, derived preview_kind, the Latest distribution pointer, payload density, runtime form, and task mode are independent. promote_quality and move_latest_pointer are separate operations; pointer movement never changes quality.

release_platform_matrix.selection_boundary: workflow_callers_pass_only_audited_policy_or_platform_ids_and_the_canonical_source_resolver_emits_build_json; Stable optional IDs are canonicalized into the pre-issued authority, copied into the run-bound operation control, preserved in the Standard checkpoint, and consumed unchanged by the post-success follower

provider_configuration_boundary.rule: Provider configuration is optional local use-time configuration. Release build, Manual Full M1, local delivery, Preview publication, and managed package currentness never require a Provider credential. A specifically requested connected VM diagnostic may automatically reuse the selected OPL Gateway Base URL and bearer token from the developer host Codex config; it never asks the release user for a duplicate credential and never generates a synthetic API key.

github_release_name.rule: GitHub Release names, tags, assets, and UI use the display version. Updater, app package metadata, CFBundle versions, and Homebrew ordering use the separately bound machine version; Stable revisions are independent immutable releases.

local_install.install_handoff: quit the running cn.onepersonlab.opl process, replace /Applications/One Person Lab.app with the exact build App, clear quarantine when present, and relaunch
local_install.authority_boundary: The local-install profile builds and verifies one exact local App/Shell/Framework cohort for this Mac only. It cannot publish or promote a release, write GHCR or Homebrew, require notarization, or stand in for public distribution readiness. It cannot claim clean-VM or attestation evidence.

framework_authority.rule: OPL Framework owns the generic immutable Release Bundle schema, store, canonical digest, receipts, operation events, consumer envelopes, and executor ABI. The App consumes that authority and must not fork or redefine its closed shape.

identity.prebuild_rule: A new App Standard artifact records exact App, Shell, and Framework source refs only as reproducible build provenance. Those refs and the resulting Bundle digest never gate installation or runtime composition with external Base or Packages. Compatibility is admitted only by capability, minimum version, or SemVer range; historical Bundles remain read-compatible.

required_frozen_bindings: prepared notes when required by the track
freeze_admission.binding_authority: manual source lock or immutable Framework Release Bundle

post_freeze_validation.authority: frozen checkout tree, source lock, Bundle, artifact bytes, and bound digests

cohort_invalidation_causes: frozen byte tree or digest mismatch
explicit security revocation bound to the frozen ref or digest
source_freeze_currentness_policy.rule: Read remote/current authority once at freeze admission, then stop fetching or chasing moving refs. Build and qualification consume only the frozen source lock or Bundle and its task-local projections. Live catalog, main, tag, installed, or effective advancement cannot force a rebuild; only frozen-byte drift, artifact failure, or an explicit security revocation can invalidate the cohort.

live_authority.rule: Framework checkpoint state plus one App-owned Stable executor is the only live release mutation path. Daily validation uses the no-secret Canary and cannot authorize, schedule, dispatch, publish, rebuild, promote, or cancel.

event_delivery.recovery_entry: opl release status then exact opl release reconcile
event_delivery.rule: Release progress is carried by Framework receipts, events, checkpoints, and consumer envelopes. A conversation may observe and route one executable next action, but it cannot become the durable controller or keep polling after its owned operation is terminal.

freeze_adapter_rederives_from_current_op: Shell source commit and AionCore managed manifest/lock
Framework source commit and Release Set
seven Package manifests and payload manifests

protected_environment_control.rule: The release-stable environment must retain exactly one main branch policy. Daily Codex credentials cannot rewrite this verifier, and no legacy cancel or session surface can authorize a mutation. Any historical deviation requires a durable containment receipt and immediate GET-verified restoration before another Framework Bundle operation.

repository_immutability_window.owner: release-stable protected environment unique Release owner

notes_required_statements: This is not Stable and is not an automatic update.
Stable Latest, updater metadata, Homebrew, and the Standard checkpoint remain unchanged.

ghcr.rule: GHCR WebUI publication is not silently omitted: it is explicitly outside the desktop Stable Latest gate and retains its independent App-owned publication and runtime readback.

legacy_compatibility.rule: Legacy App session, broker, and operator implementations are absent. Historical evidence remains readable through the retained Bundle status commands and JSON contracts; no legacy implementation can create state or authorize a live release action.

release_execution_tracks.purpose: Execution location is an implementation choice, not a product, channel, asset, updater, or release-note difference.

local.role: fast development, debugging, build, same-artifact qualification, and explicitly authorized publication fallback
local.handoff_rule: Publish or hand off the exact qualified artifact set; do not rebuild merely to change execution track.

remote.role: routine Stable publication and continuous reproducibility proof after the remote pipeline is stable

development_isolation.release_source: immutable detached checkout or release-owned worktree
development_isolation.release_freeze_scope: exact cohort checkout, artifact bytes, and bounded remote mutation window only
development_isolation.rule: Packaging reads frozen source bytes. It must never reserve the development root, freeze unrelated worktrees, or require normal development to wait for build, VM, upload, or remote verification.

stable.target_reader: ordinary App users and release operators deciding whether to install, upgrade, promote, or troubleshoot the Stable package

nightly.target_reader: opt-in testers evaluating an automated Standard preview
nightly.comparison: current frozen App Shell Framework cohort without a Stable qualification claim

template_policy.rule: Template release notes preserve evidence facts and technical details only when the operator requested a dry-run or diagnostic preview and must not replace prepared Stable copy. Automated Nightly uses a separate fixed scope-and-risk disclosure that cannot claim Stable qualification, Full, WebUI, Latest, or heavy-VM completion.

public_release_notes.public_asset_policy: Release-note evidence JSON and technical audit output are operator evidence, not public download assets; the public GitHub Release asset list stays focused on install, update, checksum, and manifest entrypoints.
public_release_notes.rule: Public release notes use prepared user copy derived from script-generated evidence before the expensive release train starts. Publish and promote jobs must not call AI to generate or replace notes on the critical path. The body leads with user scenarios, upgrade value, and action items; commit logs, refs, workflow facts, changelog details, and packaging audit material belong in Technical details or evidence artifacts instead of the main narrative.

dmg_compression.metadata_blockmap_gate: node --experimental-strip-types scripts/validate-release.ts release-assets plus focused hdiutil imageinfo/verify readback from a standard macOS build artifact
dmg_compression.rule: Standard macOS DMG uses electron-builder-supported ULFO by default because electron-builder 26.8.1 does not accept ULMO in dmg.format. ULMO for standard assets requires a separate postprocess patch that proves canonical updater metadata, ZIP blockmap, and latest-arm64-mac.yml still match the published assets before it can replace the default; latest-mac.yml and DMG blockmap files are legacy compatibility assets only when deliberately published.

production_distribution_override.rule: Production Standard publication requires Developer ID, accepted notarization, stapler validation, Gatekeeper, and exact public-byte readback.

macos_app_bundle_trust.verification: npm run verify-remote-release on macos-latest downloads the public DMG, ZIP, and unified release attestation; it binds exact SHA-256 bytes, validates embedded Gatekeeper and notarization evidence, validates the stapled DMG, mounts the App, extracts the updater App, and requires Developer ID codesign plus Gatekeeper acceptance on both App copies.
macos_app_bundle_trust.rule: Production Standard updater replacement is fail-closed: Developer ID, accepted notarization, stapling, Gatekeeper, and exact public-byte evidence are mandatory; local authorization and ad-hoc signatures are non-distributable.

standard_updater.rule: standard updater metadata is canonical arm64-only latest-arm64-mac.yml, must never point to Full first-install assets, and must bind the final notarized Standard DMG plus Developer ID updater ZIP; latest-mac.yml is a legacy compatibility alias only when deliberately published.

draft_refresh.scope: standard App DMG, ZIP, ZIP blockmap, canonical arm64 updater metadata, Gatekeeper policy, and Apple notarization receipt before Stable promotion

local_data_lifecycle.policy_surface: Settings / Storage and Settings / Updates & Maintenance

storage_inventory.rule: Storage inventory must show App-managed local data roots and cleanup modes before any destructive action. It is the required readback surface before archive, prune, rotation, or cache cleanup execution.

updater_cache.rule: Updater cache cleanup may delete stale downloaded installer packages, but must preserve pending recovery metadata and the currently selected update package until install is applied or replaced. Retired updater cache roots are no longer active install roots and may remove downloaded installer packages while preserving recovery metadata and non-package files.

logs.rule: Logs may be bounded or cleaned through a user-visible maintenance action, but log cleanup must not be used as proof that user artifacts were retained, archived, or removed.

user_data_artifacts.rule: Conversations, workspaces, generated artifacts, results, papers, baselines, reports, and narrative/intermediate deliverables are user data artifacts. The App must not silently delete them; cleanup requires inventory, archive/export, restore-proof, and explicit user confirmation.

runtime_substrate.rule: Storage inventory shows both the active-shell toolchain runtime and the OPL managed runtime, but prune authority belongs only to the OPL managed runtime. Prune starts as a dry-run, fails closed without a valid current pointer and install marker, and may only target unreferenced marker-backed runtime generations.

nightly_standard.rule: Nightly production defaults to the daily schedule. A user-explicit development_validation may invoke workflow_dispatch with the exact publish_nonlatest_nightly confirmation and must execute the same scheduled Nightly path. The frozen request, qualification, publication receipt, and followers bind the invocation mode, event, authority source, exact run, and cohort. Neither mode publishes Full or WebUI or changes Latest. A separate explicit protected single-use exact-CAS operation may move Latest to the published Nightly without changing Preview quality; the next qualified Stable reclaims by default.

webui_full.rule: Latest and its Stable compatibility alias must point to the same qualified payload-capable WebUI runtime image. A metadata-only image may not be promoted as the beginner default.

webui_slim.rule: Slim images may carry only WebUI, AionCore, bootstrap, and seed metadata, but must not be tagged stable or documented as the default beginner path.

runtime_image_contract.rule: Docker/WebUI starts as a preheated WebUI runtime image: the image gets users to a browser quickly, while OPL Framework owns reconciliation and managed updates inside the mounted /data state.

github_package_access.configuration_surface: GitHub Packages settings Manage Actions access
github_package_access.public_api_policy: GitHub does not expose a stable public REST or GraphQL endpoint for configuring personal package repository association or Actions access; configure these gates through the package settings UI.
github_package_access.rule: App-owned WebUI GHCR publishing requires the one-person-lab-webui package to be associated with gaofeng21cn/one-person-lab-app and to grant write Actions access to gaofeng21cn/one-person-lab-app before App workflows can update existing GHCR tags.

retention_policy.rule: WebUI GHCR cleanup must retain protected moving tags, recent stable/nightly versions, and declared rollback tags; deletion is never part of ordinary release publishing.

webui_ghcr_image.rule: WebUI GHCR image truth remains an App-owned server deployment concern outside the desktop Release Bundle. The desktop standard, resume_standard, and append_full operations cannot publish or move GHCR tags; a separately authorized WebUI lane must validate the runtime image and read back exact digests.

native_webui_distribution.rule: Native WebUI assets are additive post-Stable carriers. Automatic followers remain non-blocking; manual recovery is a bounded generation chain where each new run consumes the same successful Stable authority, the exact pre-publication failed first attempt, and every prior failed recovery.

cask_install_policy.rule: Homebrew user and CI installs use the fully qualified standard cask ref and trust only the standard plus conflicts_with sibling cask refs so installation stays explicit without granting broad trust to the whole tap.

tap_update_policy.direct_commit_conflict_policy: Push once, then compare exact local and remote tap commits; an unknown or mismatched result fails closed without retry, rerun, or redispatch

homebrew_tap_distribution.full_first_install_policy: the already-public mutable Standard GitHub Release is the exact same-tag append target; workflow asset name+digest CAS and the unified public attestation bind the Full DMG and manifest. The protected Homebrew Full follower consumes those exact same-tag assets with digest CAS and public readback; physical clean-machine certification remains optional and non-blocking; no independent Full release or tag is created, and the Standard assets, release body, Latest, and updater metadata remain unchanged

production_macos_trust.rule: Production Full publication fails closed unless the exact final stapled DMG bytes bind Developer ID, Apple notarization Accepted, stapler validation, Gatekeeper, and passed nested native runtime trust.

codex_cli.version_source: OPL Codex-only projection derived from AionCore producer manifest
codex_cli.verification: The active AionUI shell must resolve one exact Codex executable from the bundled-aioncore managed-resources Codex-only projection and pass it through OPL_CODEX_BIN; the final App tree must prove Claude absent and the Full Framework runtime must prove all forbidden duplicate paths absent.

temporal_cli.verification: App-owned runtime/current/bin/temporal must satisfy minimum_version, execute offline from the packaged archive wrapper, and pass Temporal provider smoke; system PATH/Homebrew/global Temporal may be reported as diagnostics but is not the default runtime source

managed_commands: opl family-runtime service supervisor status --provider temporal
opl family-runtime service supervisor install --provider temporal
opl family-runtime service supervisor trigger --provider temporal
temporal_runtime_provider.verification: Full manifest runtime_assertions.temporal_core_bridge_releases must be exactly aarch64-apple-darwin, runtime_assertions.offline_required_payloads must prove the macOS arm64 SWC native binding, wrapper must export local Temporal defaults, and the same-run Full qualification receipt must bind a passed opl_temporal_service_supervisor_proof.v1

bun_cli.verification: Full manifest optional_components.bun records packaged or not_packaged status

size_policy.goal: Keep Full first-install complete and offline-capable while making size growth visible and reviewable.

threshold_semantics.above_review_threshold_rule: A Full DMG above the review threshold must open package-size review and optimization planning, but it must not authorize removing required offline first-install payloads.
threshold_semantics.stable_release_coupling_rule: Full DMG warning or review-threshold status is not release-blocking by size alone and must not block stable clean evidence unless a hard size limit, uncompressed runtime limit, offline payload boundary, native trust, or Full clean VM smoke gate fails.
threshold_semantics.cache_hit_rule: A Full runtime cache hit only proves reusable package assembly input; it is never App release readiness, runtime dependency truth, or OPL family production readiness.

optimization_artifacts.rule: Optimization evidence is part of the Full package manifest/readback surface and may only prove explicit non-runtime pruning plus boundary preservation. Full clean VM smoke is separately classified as post-publication optional certification and must never appear in package_optimization.required_evidence or block publication.

standard.role: ordinary App package and standard updater target

full.role: clean-machine first-install package with bundled runtime payloads

offline_kit.role: manual diagnostic/runtime recovery artifact that consumes the same OPL runtime bundle manifest boundary

opl_full_runtime.role: offline first-install runtime payload assembled from the OPL runtime bundle manifest; dependency truth remains in OPL

aionui_bundled_runtime.role: AionUI shell runtime required by the App bundle

measured_records.conclusion: Compression level 9 alone cannot bring the measured Full DMG back under the 750000000-byte review threshold.

optimization_priority_order.rule: Reduce duplicated runtime payloads and layer contents only when Full offline Core readiness and native trust evidence remain intact.
Remove non-runtime shell assets, maps, tests, caches, or reports without changing App-owned GUI behavior or shell authority boundaries.
Treat Electron footprint work as shell/runtime-carrier optimization; do not replace it with an unsupported carrier during release packaging.
Use compression tuning as secondary size reduction only; the v26.6.21 zlib-level=9 estimate remains above the review threshold.

draft_refresh.scope: New Full publication uses exact same-tag asset CAS against the already-public mutable Standard Release; no independent Full draft, release, tag, or parallel Latest is created.

published_addon.attestation_binding: opl-release-manifest.json binds opl-release-attestation.json digest and exact Full asset name/size/digest

release_efficiency_boundary.rule: Full runtime bundle preparation belongs to OPL Framework. The App Full release consumes the bundle manifest, lock, env contract, and readback refs and packages required offline payloads; it does not own dependency truth or add runtime materialization to the release critical path.

release_preflight.failure_budget: fail product-policy admission before Framework freeze or any expensive build; evaluate Full-specific failures only in append_full

scope: current App profile against exact Shell consumer in a temporary archive
source_gate.rule: The App release source gate runs once before dispatch and is embedded in the operator-issued authority. It records the exact App/Shell/Framework source and build provenance used to produce the selected App artifact, then verifies the frozen bytes before dependency installation or expensive hosted build, Full, WebUI, or post-publication optional certification work. These refs are observational build provenance only and never an install/runtime compatibility gate.

release_preflight.rule: The App freeze-request adapter validates product identity, selected App artifact identity, Framework compatibility requirements, prepared Standard notes, and typed Package compatibility, then hands one app_standard_compatibility request to Framework freeze without Package Release Set or exact Package authority fields. It cannot create release state or replace Framework checkpoint admission; App/Shell/Framework source refs remain provenance only, and append_full remains independently admissible with historical Bundle identity read-compatible.

status_semantics.passed: started certification completed successfully with immutable evidence
status_semantics.failed: started certification completed with a product or quality failure
status_semantics.not_run: no certification job started; an explicit non-execution reason may be sealed
status_semantics.unavailable: a started certification job failed typed lease, VM, or capability admission

post_publication_optional_certification.rule: Optional clean-machine certification consumes the exact already-published artifact and produces a separate immutable receipt. It never rebuilds, mutates or resigns the component manifest, blocks publication or Latest, or masquerades as publication success.

release_acceleration.rule: Acceleration may change latency or diagnostic coverage only. It cannot create release state, authorize mutation, skip a Framework checkpoint stage, or change artifact identity.

routine_advisory.rule: Routine advisory runs only for one admitted immutable successful main validation source. Every target is admitted independently; unavailable capacity produces a typed not_run receipt without queueing or affecting Stable, Latest, or merge availability.

runner_policy.rule: Self-hosted runners add platform evidence and development throughput but are never a Stable or Latest availability dependency. Fleet leases coordinate physical machines; GitHub Actions owns runner registration and scheduling; neither control plane may be inferred from the other's inventory alone.

cache_policy.truth_boundary: Cache presence, restore hits, misses, writes, and cleanup receipts are acceleration evidence only; they cannot claim artifact identity, release readiness, owner approval, stable/latest publication, runtime truth, or domain truth.

bootstrap_only.purpose: fast App launch and bootstrap blocker capture before rerunning a full release train
keeps: wrapper smoke command and log artifacts

release_gate.purpose: full deterministic VM qualification used only when an explicit diagnostic or optional certification workflow requests it
keeps: wrapper smoke command and log artifacts
release_gate.critical_failure_artifact_policy: write vm-gate-failure-summary.json/md before uploading large VM artifacts; classify missing large artifacts separately as diagnostic_artifact_missing and recommend rerun_diagnostic_same_artifact
release_gate.wrapper_diagnostic_policy: host_wrapper_preflight_and_smoke_logs are supporting evidence; deterministic VM readiness/settings/route/codex failures classify the optional certification result only

writes: temporary standard DMG diagnostic artifact only

first_run_vm_concurrency.rule: Scheduled VM smokes collapse stale backlog and default to a focused bootstrap-launch diagnostic; stable release-called VM profiles must use run/profile-scoped groups so standard, Homebrew, and Full install gates cannot cancel or replace each other.

scheduled_release_bundle_activity_guard.rule: Scheduled maintenance must not occupy the self-hosted first-run VM runner while a Stable or Nightly Bundle operation is active, queued, or cannot be checked.

first_run_vm_artifact_handoff.source_run_download_command: actions/download-artifact@v8 with run-id=<release_artifact_run_id || github.run_id> and name=<release_artifact_name>
first_run_vm_artifact_handoff.rule: Branch-lane or post-release evidence runs may explicitly download a DMG-only artifact from a completed source Actions run without publishing assets; this handoff is optional VM evidence only and must not replace hosted publication-floor checks or published asset verification.

tart_base_prebake.truth_boundary: prebaked Tart base can reduce host setup latency only; clean App install, first launch, Settings smoke, assistant route smoke, and release readiness still come from the VM smoke artifact

key_invalidation_scope.toolchain: toolchain bytes, versions, source-tree fingerprints, toolchain builder implementation, and toolchain prune projection
key_invalidation_scope.domain-runtime: selected package dependency closure, copied source fingerprints, domain builder implementation, and modules prune projection
key_invalidation_scope.opl-runtime: Framework runtime bytes, production dependency closure, OPL builder implementation, and opl prune projection
key_invalidation_scope.skills: selected package-set identity, OPL Flow workflow policy when selected, App product profile, selected skill bytes, skills packager implementation, and skills prune projection

full_dmg_compression.rule: Stable Full CI uses ULMO for the App-owned fallback/rebuilt DMG path by default. UDZO remains available as a legacy diagnostic override with zlib level 9 by default. Release readiness still records compressed Full DMG size from the published GitHub asset; crossing the review threshold opens package-size review but does not authorize removing required offline first-install payloads.

full_runtime_packaging_hygiene.policy_summary_boundary: This release contract records the policy owner and evidence surfaces only. Runtime tree filters, package filters, app-bundle trim rules, protected payloads, validation examples, and expected absent paths are not duplicated here; they live in the source_of_truth contract and must be read through the policy audit.
full_runtime_packaging_hygiene.app_policy: exclude local indexes, dependency caches, tests, package docs/fixtures/examples, Python stdlib tests, and user/runtime state; do not prune declared offline first-install payloads, Codex/Temporal archives, domain modules, or packaged skills; do not infer domain truth or artifact authority from package pruning

vm_local_authorization_policy.rule: Stable first-run VM smokes must clear quarantine after install, record codesign and spctl diagnostics before launch, and continue when codesign or spctl rejects the unsigned locally authorized App.

settings_page_readiness_policy.rule: Settings VM readiness is semantic and structural. User-facing copy may change without failing a healthy packaged page; route, stable page anchor, navigation, nonempty content, and absence of blocking loading or first-run layers remain release-blocking.

settings_runtime_refresh_evidence_policy.rule: Production Settings smoke must exercise both the legacy Settings Runtime alias and the standalone Runtime route with independent requested/resolved route identity, structural readiness, and pre/post refresh idle evidence. Synthetic target injection may support unit tests but cannot satisfy the production release gate.

assistant_route_smoke_policy.runtime_target_resolution: resolve every fixture target from fresh app_state.agent_packages.directory.entries and status_index.home_shortcut_preferences before probing
assistant_route_smoke_policy.rule: Standard proves that every release qualification target resolves from fresh Framework projections and that an unavailable projected professional Agent Package remains selectable while send stays blocked with a repair path. Full applies the selected project directory as session cwd and future domain workspace identity, creates the conversation through the visible composer without Shell package activation, then reads that conversation back. Separately, a real Framework domain StageRun or StageAttempt must activate from its own workspace_locator and emit matching runtime evidence. Direct conversation POSTs, Shell send-boundary activation, and synthetic runtime or route evidence cannot satisfy the Full gate. The fixture never creates runtime catalog, visibility, lifecycle, readiness, action, or install authority, and a Standard launch gate must never be counted as a Full route receipt.

vm_gates.precondition: VM image already has Homebrew installed

ai_exploratory_policy.rule: AI-assisted exploratory UI checks can discover issues but cannot block or clear release readiness without a deterministic gate.

nightly_standard.purpose: automatic scheduled Standard prerelease using the shared physical build with no Stable Latest or heavy-VM authority

stable.purpose: publish one CAS- and attestation-protected mutable Standard through the GitHub-hosted source, contract, build, signing, notarization, package, Homebrew, Latest, repository-setting restore, and public readback floor
stable.heavy_gate_policy: post-publication optional certification never blocks or queues Stable publication or Latest
forbidden_inferences: stable/latest promotion from draft evidence bundle alone
family production readiness from App release/user-path evidence
MAS/MAG/RCA/OBF domain readiness from App release/user-path evidence
runtime truth from App UI rendering

release_cohort.rule: A release evidence bundle can support packaged App evidence only when every artifact belongs to the same App release cohort. Partial readouts may preserve an unknown cohort, but passed bundles must declare release_cohort and the remote verification artifact must match its version/tag.

required_artifacts.producer: packaged GUI Codex post-install functional check

conditional_artifacts.producer: Runtime page minimal work-item status screenshot

optional_diagnostic_artifacts.producer: packaged GUI Codex AI-first post-install self-check

operator_evidence_bundle.acceptance_rule: App records and displays cohort-bound refs-only release evidence produced by OPL/runtime/domain owners; it does not reinterpret the bundle as runtime truth, domain truth, artifact authority, a quality verdict, stable/latest promotion, or family production readiness.

can_support: Runtime page minimal visual acceptance for the same release cohort
packaged GUI route smoke for the same release cohort
App release owner promotion review input
cannot_support: stable/latest promotion without explicit release owner decision

release_owner_verdict.next_owner_action: record release_owner_verdict_ref or release_owner_receipt_ref for the same App release cohort, or record release_owner_typed_blocker_ref, typed_blocker_ref, or human_gate_ref when release-ready cannot be authorized
release_owner_verdict.rule: Same-cohort release and user-path evidence can feed App release-owner review, but an owner verdict is evidence only. It cannot dispatch, rerun, cancel, publish, promote, or change Framework checkpoint state, and it cannot independently claim release-ready.

managed_update_plane.status_consumption_policy: App consumes status, conditions, progress refs, and repair action refs only; App does not implement OPL Base or OPL Packages mutation.

software_lifecycle.carrier_alignment_rule: Carrier choice does not change software-object identity or lifecycle authority. Full carriers may seed payloads, but Framework lifecycle owns Base and Packages activation, reconciliation, update, repair, rollback, and uninstall.

user_experience.silent_apply_when: Framework plan auto_apply.eligible and app_background_safe are true and command_ref is present
user_experience.attention_when: Framework skips a dirty, developer, user-managed, global, incompatible, or verification-failed target
